chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about false testifiers. He (peace be upon him) said: 'They are whipped with a penalty (hadd) that has no fixed time, and that is upon the Imam (peace be upon him), and they are paraded until the people recognize them.'
And as for the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And do not accept any testimony from them ever... Except those who repent'.

He (peace be upon him) said. I said, 'How is their repentance recognized?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He lies about himself before the chiefs of the people until he is whipped, and he seeks Forgiveness of his Lord. And when he does that, so his repentance has been manifested.'
ai.seo_question: What is the punishment and criteria for repentance of false witnesses in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the penal procedure for false witnesses, emphasizing the Imam's discretion in administering lashes and the public parading (tazhir) to ensure communal recognition of their guilt. It clarifies the Quranic exception for repentance by defining it as a public act of self-condemnation until the punishment is executed, thereby restoring their credibility for future testimony.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Zurara, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked himasws about false testifiers’. So heasws said: ‘They would be whipped the Penalty (Hadd). There is not (fixed) time for it, and that is upon the Imamasws, and they would be paraded with until the the people recognise them’.
And as for the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [24:4] and do not accept any testimony from them ever . . . . [24:5] Except those who repent

, I said, ‘How is their repentance recognised?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would belie himself (confess) to the chiefs of the people until he is whipped, and he would seek Forgiveness of his Lord<sup>azwj</sup>’. And when he does that, so his repentance would have been manifested’.
